messages.content: 我2000平方英尺的房子需要多少電力？

function.name: solar_panel_calculate_need
function.description: Calculate the number of solar panels needed for a house based on the square footage and average sunlight hours. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

square_footage.description: The square footage of the house. This is a float type value.

average_sunlight_hours.description: The average hours of sunlight received. This is a float type value.

usage_efficiency.description: The efficiency of energy usage in the home, default is 0.8. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "I have a 2000 square foot house, how much electricity do I need?" They want an estimate of power consumption? We can provide approximate daily or monthly consumption. But we might also ask clarifying question about location, climate, appliances, etc. But maybe they want a quick estimate. We can give typical consumption per square foot. For US, average residential consumption ~ 10 kWh per square foot per year? Actually typical US household uses ~10kWh per day? Wait typical US household uses ~900 kWh per month (~30 days) -> 30 kWh per day. For 2000 sq ft, that's 15 kWh per 1000 sq ft per month? Let's compute: 900 kWh/month / 2000 sq ft = 0.45 kWh per sq ft per month. That seems low. Actually typical US consumption ~ 10,000 kWh per year for 1500 sq ft -> 6.7 kWh per sq ft per year. So for 2000 sq ft, ~13,400 kWh/year. That's ~1,117 kWh/month. That's ~37 kWh/day. So we can say around 40 kWh per day. Then we can convert to solar panel requirement: using the function. Provide square footage 2000, average sunlight hours maybe 5 hours, usage efficiency default 0.8. Use function.
